The pCO out 2 2 and pCO in pressures were controlled by the height of the water column to 1.1 psi, 2 which is the indication of a constant pressure value inside the CO chamber. A 2 galvanostatic current was applied at 125 mA/cm2 (12.5 A total current to the 100 cm2 reactor). As indicated in Figure 21, the faradaic efficiency remained high and stable, with FE ≥ 85% (target value = 75%) for the evaluated duration (215 hours). The total cell voltage during this duration is in the range of 4.2-4.4 V. Throughout the test, the pressures remained constant and in the following ranges: 28 • CO side pressure of the GDE: pCO out = 1.09-1.10psi (CO chamber) 2 2 2 • Catholyte inlet pressure of the catholyte side of GDE: pCin = 0.25 – 1.25 psi (inlet catholyte) • Catholyte outlet pressure on the side of GDE with catholyte, this comprises catholyte and some CO gas: pCout = 0.60-0.80psi (outlet catholyte) 2 Unlike previous tests, no GDE cracking was detected up to the current completed period of 265 hours, the endpoint of the experiment confirming that the constant CO 2 chamber pressure mode of operation works suitably. With this experiment, OCOchem demonstrated the small cell of 100 cm2 area (10 cm x 10 cm) at a current density of 125 mA/cm2, achieving CO to formate conversion faradaic efficiency at 85% (significantly 2 above the 70% BP2 target) with negligible flooding for 265 hours of operation at a 4.5 V cell voltage (5% above the 4.2V BP2 target). As indicated in Figure 22 (a), pressure in the CO chamber is maintained constant by the water column, as shown by the 2 constant value over time of the pCO out pressure. The total cell voltage (Vcell) 2 increases from an initial value of 4.2V to 4.4V over 50 hours and then stays nearly constant during the duration of the test (Figure 22 (b)). The increase is potentially due to gas diffusion electrode (GDE) wetting initially with the voltage/current being applied and then reaching an equilibrium where there is sufficient porosity for CO to be transported 2 across the GDE while maintaining the same wetting and no further increase. The negative sign for the Vcell is the result of the instrument sign convention.
